scope: Implemented config/reward budget, with assumed human behavior and pre-change measured route timings; not observed human completion times. Physics signatures and unchanged route dependencies checked.

mastery.eligibility: A full actual forward main/ridge traversal of a configured fork before a successful loaded non-test delivery. Counted once per run, not once per fork. Target number alone never grants it.
mastery.rounding: Each bonus component floors independently through production calculateDeliveryReward.

retention.normalModel: Exact mission-state probability propagation per successful delivery, using measured crossedBridges, persistent distinct bridge IDs and independent assumed clean/hard outcomes. Mission progress does not transfer to the next mission in that run.
retention.first: One-time only per canonical delivered checkpoint; finite bonuses from visited endpoints only.
retention.skip: Free skip resets progress. Repeating three-delivery mission pays90cash20brains per3successes; late repeated bridge or hard missions may pay more. Absolute modeled bound150cash40brains per success is deliberately generous.

modelNotes: Restarts, human speed factor, failure probabilities, failure location, clean fraction and hard selection are assumptions. Only clean route seconds/fuel/reward/bridges were measured. Hard main versus alternate timing differences are not remeasured here.

Each simulation purchases an integer count of expected successful deliveries. Expected failed attempts per success = p/(1-p); failure time =0.65 of slowed route. Failure pays no delivery/first/mission reward, while ordinary movement brains accrue.

Integer production reward rounding is used before averaging probabilities. Expected rewards may be fractional, so these are budgeting trajectories, not sampled complete careers or an estimate of population means.

Driving earns cash and brains concurrently. Upgrade builds are paid before their measured route is used; real stock deliveries fill any brain shortfall. No forced school waiting or extra clock is inserted.
Typical purchased upgrades are fuel10 and speed/handling/grip3; all other cars, skins, schools and fullmax upgrades are optional.
No debug cash, save edits, offline earnings, trade-in revenue or mandatory progression locks. Existing saved money and purchases are preserved; this model starts a fresh career.
The16destinations and repeated shared early road still mean repetition. New goals and small bonuses do not establish fun, a3–8minute reward cadence, or a7–8hour human mean without playtests.
